title: Token pass-through: a signed assertion, verified twice
lede: A front-end application acting as an agent mints a short-lived signed assertion naming the end user, itself and the target backend. The gateway verifies it and forwards it unchanged; the backend verifies it again and scopes its answer to the end user. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

steps.title: A user asks the front-end
steps.what: The front-end application serves the user and needs to call a backend on their behalf.

steps.title: It signs an assertion
steps.what: It mints a short-lived assertion: the end user, itself, the target backend, a lifetime and a unique id.

steps.title: Signed with RS256
steps.what: The signature is real, from a throwaway RSA key generated locally.

steps.title: It calls the gateway
steps.what: The assertion travels in the request. The agent-side code never learns any backend credential.

steps.title: The gateway verifies
steps.what: Signature, issuer, audience and expiry. A wrong audience, an expired token, a tampered payload, an untrusted issuer or alg none are refused here.

steps.title: Forwarded unchanged
steps.what: The mock gateway hands on the same string; the page compares a digest of what the backend received with the one minted. That shows what the mock does: a gateway that rewrote the token would also fail the backend's signature check.

steps.title: The backend verifies for itself
steps.what: It checks the signature and audience again and refuses a replayed id.

steps.title: A scoped answer
steps.what: Because the assertion names the end user, the backend returns only what that user may see.
